elements.quote: This SRMA has comprised of two main outcomes. The primary outcome was magnitude of SSI among women underwent cesarean section, which is defined as the proportion of women after cesarean section who fulfills the CDC criteria of surgical site definition within 30 days of post-partum and it could be at least one of the following: ( A superficial incisional , deep incisional or deep/organ SSI) . The secondary outcome was the determinants of SSI after cesarean section in Ethiopia.
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly lists and defines the outcome domains: primary outcome (magnitude of SSI with CDC definition and types) and secondary outcome (determinants).

elements.quote: Inclusion. This SRMA included all articles conducted in all regional state of Ethiopia reporting the prevalence/proportion/incidence of SSI after cesarean section and/or associated factors. All observational study designs (case-control and cross-sectional study designs) were included in this SRMA. Both published articles and grey literatures published in English language from January 1 2013 to September 2023. Exclusion. which lack our outcome of interest: SSI following cesarean section and its predictors were excluded from this SRMA. On the other hand, literatures with poor quality as per the criteria of reviewing articles were excluded from this SRMA.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes overall inclusion and exclusion criteria (population, study designs, time frame, language, outcome) used to select studies for the review, but it does not describe the processes used to decide which studies were eligible for each specific synthesis (for example, how studies were tabulated and compared to planned groups for each synthesis or how studies were chosen for different subgroup/meta-analyses).

elements.quote:
All the datasets were exported to Mendeley reference manager, and then we transferred to the Microsoft Excel spreadsheet to remove duplicate data in the review. Two authors (ES and MA) independently extracted all the important data using standardized data extraction format developed according to 2014 Joanna Briggs Institute (JBI) Reviewers' manual [24]. ... The name of the author, sample size, publication year, study region, study design, prevalence/proportion of surgical site infection, and adjusted odds ratio with its 95% CI of the factors associated with SSI.

The extracted Microsoft Excel spreadsheet format data was imported to STATA software version 17 (STATA corporation, Texas, USA) for analysis. Then random effect model was used to estimate the pooled prevalence of SSI after cesarean section in Ethiopia. ... A forest plot format was used to present the pooled prevalence of surgical site infection after cesarean section with 95% CI. To identify determinant factors, we used the pooled AOR in forest plot format with its respective 95%CI.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes data management steps (exporting references, transferring to Excel, standardized extraction of author, sample size, prevalence and adjusted ORs with 95% CI) and that Excel data were imported into STATA for meta-analysis and presentation (forest plots). However, it does not describe methods for preparing summary statistics when missing (e.g., imputations, conversions between effect measures, calculating SE/CI from other statistics) or specific data conversion procedures. Therefore preparation steps are reported but handling of missing summary statistics or conversions is not described.

elements.quote: The name of the author, sample size, publication year, study region, study design, prevalence/proportion of surgical site infection, and adjusted odds ratio with its 95% CI of the factors associated with SSI.
elements.reason: The manuscript describes the standardized data extraction format and explicitly lists the data items extracted (author, sample size, year, region, design, prevalence, AOR with 95% CI), and notes transfer to an Excel spreadsheet for processing, which specifies the tabular data and structure used.

elements.quote: Funnel plot and Eggers test were done to assess publication bias. ... elements.quote: Subgroup analysis was done based on the study region.

elements.quote: Funnel plot and Eggers test were done to assess publication bias. ... A forest plot format was used to present the pooled prevalence of surgical site infection after cesarean section with 95% CI.

elements.quote: Therefore we have used the random effect model to resolve the issue of heterogeneity between included studies.

elements.quote: Then random effect model was used to estimate the pooled prevalence of SSI after cesarean section in Ethiopia.
